cells.tense: The first clear sight is here and you are meeting it without holding on.
cells.ask: Take one minute with one person this week and say one thing you notice — just one. Then stop. Say it as your own observation, not a diagnosis, and let it sit.
cells.core:
You're in the room between you and someone else, taking in what's there before deciding what it means. You're not certain yet, and that's the useful part — you can look at something fully without having settled it. Most people can't sit in that spot for long. They name it, fix it, or move on. You can, and it lets you stay close to someone while you're still unsure about them.

The pull to name or brace for what's next is real, and some of it is in the room with you. Nothing here says you're behind. Let your next move come from what you actually took in, not from the pressure to sound sure. One notice, one person, then let it sit.
cells.sheetLine: You can look before you decide what it means.
cells.verb: seeing what's in front of you before a name arrives
cells.place: the room between you and someone else, where you feel with them and stay with what's there

cells.tense: You are bracing for what the sight will mean and racing past the moment in front of you.
cells.ask: With one person this week, say what you notice and then add nothing. Let the next minute be theirs. No advice, no follow-up — just the observation and the quiet.
cells.core:
You're looking harder than anyone asked, as if looking owes you a conclusion. What's dawning is light, not a lever — you can't steer it by rehearsing where it goes. You're already at the end, mapping what it means, what to do, what they'll say, and the hurry is aimed at a future you can't write in.

When this is working, you notice one thing and let it stay a moment before you act on it. That's available now, and it takes less than a minute. If you say what you see out loud once and then go quiet, the moment stays fresh instead of being resolved on your behalf. Nothing has to be handled today.

cells.tense: You stopped letting yourself look first, and you are not sure when that happened.
cells.ask: One person this week, before you know what to say: tell them one thing you notice, out loud. Don't soften it into a feeling — just what you see. Then leave it alone.
cells.core:
Something in you stopped offering the first look. You're with people, you care about them, and you're not taking them in the way you once did when you were right there with them. When this is working, one plain observation is enough — you say what's in front of you without hedging it into a feeling, and it lands because you meant it.

One directed act, done for one person, and things start moving again. Not fixing, not interpreting, just saying what's there. If stepping forward feels like too much today, saying one true thing about someone you're with is still the whole ask, and it can be small.

cells.tense: You are already seeing what's in front of you and calling it something other than yours.
cells.ask: Notice one moment this week when you were first to see something and say it was you — one sentence to one person, or out loud to the room. Put your name on it.
cells.core:
There's a new clarity coming through, and you're describing it as maybe the meeting or the moment. People feel it when they're with you — a first cut before the rest gets sorted — and you keep handing the credit to the room. The recognition is already happening; the saying-so isn't. When it's working, you wake up inside the moment and you know you're the one who's there for it.

You're already moving from this. You just leave your name off it. Let one fresh notice this week land as yours — you were the one who saw it. Not a big claim, just the plain one.

attempts.check: The record puts seeing before content, so the unsupported claim would be any hint that this person has already seen something particular or that the clarity has a specific object. The reader could reasonably say the seeing is woven into everyone around them, not only in this room, and my examples may narrow it too far. The asks survive being wrong: each is visible, finishable today, and teaches something even if the read misses. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'it's the seeing itself, before any content' — I've kept it out of the cells and left it to the map.
